$comment: Documented, EXPIRING exceptions for scripts/audit-gate.mjs. Every advisory
still fails CI unless it is listed here by its GHSA id and unexpired.
An entry is a risk decision with a date on it, not a mute button: when
`expires` passes the gate goes red again so the decision gets remade.
Never add an entry to make a build green — add it only when there is no
upstream fix AND the exposure is understood and written down.

accepted.reason: Infinite-loop DoS in image-size's ICNS/JXL/HEIF parsers, reached via @molecule/api-export-pptx -> pptxgenjs 4.0.1. NO patched version exists — the advisory lists 'Patched versions: None' and every release through the current 2.0.2 is affected, so neither a bump nor an overrides pin resolves it, and npm's suggested 'fix' is a three-major downgrade of pptxgenjs (verified 2026-08-14). MITIGATED BY REACHABILITY, not merely accepted: src/imageSafety.ts refuses those three formats at the package boundary before pptxgenjs is called, sniffing magic numbers for buffers and data URIs so a declared 'image/png' cannot smuggle HEIF past it (covered by src/__tests__/imageSafety.test.ts). The vulnerable parsers therefore receive no input through this package's API. Residual risk: an `src` URL/path is checked by extension only, since the bytes are fetched inside pptxgenjs and we never see them — a caller pointing at a remote .png that serves HEIF bytes is still exposed. Re-check for a patched image-size at expiry.

Stack exhaustion in deepmerge-ts when merging deeply RECURSIVE object graphs, reached two ways: @molecule/app-tour-shepherd -> shepherd.js 15.2.2, and @molecule/api-emails-inbound-ses -> mailparser -> html-to-text 10. Fixed upstream in deepmerge-ts 8, which neither parent accepts: shepherd.js 15.2.3 (LATEST) still declares deepmerge-ts ^7.1.5 and mailparser 3.9.15 (LATEST) still resolves html-to-text 10, so we are already on the newest release of both parents and no bump exists — npm's 'fix' is a downgrade to shepherd.js 11.2.0 and mailparser 3.9.8, trading one DoS for years of unpatched everything else (verified 2026-08-17). ACCEPTED ON REACHABILITY: the merge takes CONFIGURATION, never untrusted content. html-to-text's only calls are deepMergeWithOptionsComposeRules(defaultOptions, userOptions) and a selector-map merge — the email body is a string parsed elsewhere and never reaches deepmerge — and shepherd merges developer-authored tour config. An attacker would have to control the options object the application itself constructs. Residual risk: an app that builds html-to-text options or a Shepherd tour FROM user input could hand it a recursive graph; neither molecule package does. Re-check for a shepherd.js / html-to-text release accepting deepmerge-ts 8 at expiry.

Prototype replacement in csv-parse when BOTH columns:true AND group_columns_by_name:true are set and a duplicated __proto__ header appears in the input (advisory published 2026-09-08T18:01Z — it went red mid-release). Reached only via @molecule/api-permissions-casbin -> casbin 5.51.1 -> csv-parse 5.6.0. NO upstream fix exists at or above the pinned versions: casbin 5.51.1 is the LATEST release and npm's fixAvailable is a DOWNGRADE to casbin 5.4.1; csv-parse is patched only in 7.0.2, and forcing csv-parse 7 under casbin is a blind major bump of an indirect. MITIGATED BY REACHABILITY: casbin invokes csv-parse/sync parse(line, {delimiter, skip_empty_lines, trim, relax_quotes}) with NEITHER vulnerable option set (verified in casbin 5.51.1 lib/cjs/persist/helper.js — it parses policy lines into token ARRAYS, never objects with column mapping), so the __proto__ setter branch cannot execute through this path. Residual risk: a future casbin release that adds column mapping would re-expose it — the gate goes red again at expiry. Re-check for a casbin release accepting csv-parse 7 (or shipping the fix) at expiry, and drop this entry then.
